title: A Proclamation to Provide for the Issuance of Treasury Securities 106/1998
text:
PROCLAMATION 106/ 1998
A PROCLAMATION TO PROVIDE FOR THE ISSUANCE OF TREASURY
SECURITIES
Whereas, the development of money and capital market is essential for the promotion
of price stability, full-employment and other macro-economic objectives;
Whereas, the development of the money and capital market necessitates the
introduction of the short- term and long term debt instruments;
Whereas, the Ministry of Finance needs debt instrument to raise funds for retiring
maturing liabilities, financing expenditures from revenue inflows and covering fiscal
deficits;
Now, whereas, this Proclamation is issued to provide for the issuing of Treasury
securities:
Article 1: Short Title
This Proclamation may be cited as “the Treasury Securities Proclamation No.
106/1998”.
Article 2: Definitions
In this Proclamation, unless the context otherwise requires:
(1) “Maturity” is the period of time between the issue date of a debt instrument and
the date the instrument must be redeemed by the Ministry of Finance.
(2) “Transfer” refers to the change of ownership of an instrument from one natural
or juridical person to another;
(3) “Negotiable” in reference to an instrument, means capable of being transferred
from one investor to another;
(4) “A treasury bill” is a debt instrument that may be issued by the Ministry of
Finance with an original maturity of one year or less;
(5) “Discount “ is interest that is due only at time of redemption of the security and it
is the difference between the face value and the price of the security;
(6) “A treasury bond “ is a debt instrument that may be issued by the Ministry of
Finance with an original maturity of more than one year;
(7) “An Eritrean saving bond” is a non-negotiable debt instrument that may be issued
by the Ministry of Finance;
(8) “A serial bond” is a bond issue which all the bonds with different maturity dates;
(9) “A term bond” is a bond issued which all the bonds mature at the same time;
(10) “Ledger of National Debt” is a record of all the securities issued by the
Ministry o Finance, the holders of the securities, and other information pertaining
to the debts of the Government;
(11) “A certified security” is a debt instrument whose contract is identified by a
certificate;
(12) “An uncertified or book-entry security” is a debt instrument whose contract is
identified not by certificate but by registration on a book or computer;
(13) “A registered security” is a debt instrument whose contract identifies the
investor by name;
(14) “A bearer security” is a debt instrument that identifies the investor only by
his/her possession of the certificate rather than by printing the name of the
investor on the certificate;

(15) “National debt” is the sum of total of all outstanding government debt as of a
given point in time.
Article 3: Authority to Borrow
The Ministry of Finance is authorized to borrow funds on behalf of the Government
of Eritrea in accordance with the provisions of this Proclamation.
Article 4: Debt Ceiling
The total amount of funds, which may be borrowed by the Ministry of Finance,
including interest, may not exceed Three billion Nakfa. This ceiling may be raised by
the National Assembly.
Article 5: The Bank of Eritrea as Fiscal Agent
(1) The Bank of Eritrea shall, for the purposes of this Proclamation, act as the
agent of the Ministry of Finance.
(2) The Bank of Eritrea may charge appropriate fees for its services.
Article 6: Types of Treasury Securities
(1) The Ministry of Finance may issue Treasury bills, Treasury bonds and Eritrean
savings bonds.
(2) The Ministry of Finance may issue Treasury bills and Treasury bonds in
certificated form or in unceritificated (book-entry) form.
(3) Certificated Treasury bills and bonds may be issued in bearer or registered
forms.
(4) The Treasury bonds may be serial or term bonds.
(5) Eritrean savings bonds may be issued in registered certificated form.
Article 7: Delivery of Treasury Securities
(1) For book-entry Treasury securities, delivery to the subscribers shall be made
by the registration of the subscribers as the holder of the securities in his
securities account after his payment of the subscription price.
(2) When a new book-entry security is issued or when an existing one is
transferred, a registration certificate may be furnished to the owner. How ever,
this certificate, unlike the certificate of a certified security, serves as evidence
of registration only. It is not a negotiable instrument and can, therefore, not be
assigned of pledged.
Article 8: Transfers of Treasury Securities
(1) the contract of sale of a treasury security requires for its completion delivery
of the security by the seller to the buyer.
(2) Certificated bearer Treasury bills and bonds shall be transferred by registration
and delivery, and certificated Treasury bills and bonds shall be transferred by
endorsement.
(3) Transfers of book-entry securities shall be processed through the bank of
Eritrea pursuant to a written and signed transfer request by the holder of the

security of his authorized representative or by a court decision ordering
delivery.
(4) Delivery of a book-entry security shall be made by the Debt Management
Office of the Bank of Eritrea by deleting the registration of the security from
securities account of the person making the delivery and by registering the
security in the securities account of the person receiving the delivery.
(5) The delivery for a Treasury that is sold shall specify the financial institution
and the account of the seller to which the purchase price is to be transferred.
(6) Delivery of a Treasury security that is sold shall be made only in exchange for
payment of the purchase price, unless the delivery request given to the Debt
Management Office of the Bank of Eritrea provides otherwise. The payment
shall be made when the Debt Management Office credits the account of the
seller’s financial institution specified in the delivery request with the amount
of the purchase price.
(7) Payment, clearing and settlement procedures concerning sales of Treasury
securities shall be determined by the Bank of Eritrea.
(8) Settlement of a Treasury security transaction by delivery of the security in
exchange for full payment shall be final.
(9) Eritrean savings bonds shall be non-negotiable. However, the Ministry of
Finance shall allow early redemption of savings bonds. The Ministry shall
determine the terms of the redemption.
Article 9: Legal Validity of Book-entry Securities
(1) each Treasury bill or bond issued in book-entry form shall constitute a legally
valid and binding obligation of the Government of Eritrea subject to the terms
and conditions of the issue.
(2) Subject to the provisions of this Proclamation and other applicable laws of
Eritrea, the book-entry securities shall constitute negotiable securities.
Article 10: Denominations and Maturities of Treasury Securities
The Mnistry of Finance may issue Treasury bills; Treasury bonds and eritrean savings
bonds with different maturities and denominations, provided however, that the
maturity of a Treasury bill may not exceed one year and the maturity of a Treasury
bond may not exceed thirty (30) years.
Article 11: Exemption from Taxes
(1) The issue, transfer, discounting, re-discounting or redemption of Treasury
bills shall be exempt from payment of stamp duty and any other tax.
(2) The issue, transfer or redemption of Treasury bonds and issue or redemption
of Eritrean savings bonds shall be exempt from payment of stamp duty and
any other tax.
(3) The following shall be exempt from payment of income tax:
(a) discount of or gain on sale of a treasury bill;
(b) interest on or gain on sale of a Treasury bond; and
(c) interest on an Eritrean savings bond.
Article 12: Contents of Certificates
(1) Each certificate for a certificated bearer Treasury bill shall contain the date of
issue, the security identification number, the maturity date, the face value, the
official seal of the Ministry of Finance and the signature of the Minister of

Finance in printed facsimile form. Registered certificates shall, in addition,
identify the investors.
(2) Each certificate for a certified bearer Treasury bond shall contain the date of
issue, the security identification number, the coupon rate, the maturity date,
the face value, the official seal of Mnistry of Finance and the signature of the
Minister of Finance in printed facsimile form. Registered certificates shall, in
addition, identify the investors.
Article 13: Ledger of National Debt
(1) The Bank of Eritrea shall, as fiscal agent of the Ministry of Finance, maintain
a Ledger of National Debt.
(2) The Ledger of national Debt may be kept in manual or electronic form.
(3) All Treasury securities and their holders shall be registered on the Ledger of
the National Debt.
Article 14: Legal Acceptability of Treasury Securities as Investment Vehicles
Treasury bills and bonds shall be legally acceptable investment vehicles for insurance
companies, pension funds, provident funds, banks and other institutions.
Article 15: Forfeiture of Interest Principal
Interest and principal on Treasury that can not be paid due to fault of the holder of the
security shall credited to an interest-free account on the Books of the bank of Eritrea
for the benefit of the holder concerned. If such amounts are not collected within ten
years of the applicable due dates or maturity dates they shall be forfeited to the
Ministry of Finance.
Article 16: Delay in Payment of Principal or Interest
(1) If the amount of payment by the Ministry of finance on a Treasury security is
less than the aggregate amount of the principal, interest and other charges then
due and payable on that security, the amount shall be allocated to the payment
of charges, interest and principal, in that order.
(2) If the Ministry of finance fails to make payment of principal or interest
required under the treasury security, then, for each day that such failure
continues, the Ministry of Finance shall pay to the holder of the security, in
addition to regular interest, a default charge on the outstanding principal
amount of the security. Such default charge shall accrue daily on the basis of
an annual rate that is equal to the regular annual rate of interest of the security.
(3) If the Mnistry of Finance has failed to make payment of principal, interest or
charges required under any treasury security, then, at any subsequent time
during the continuance thereof, the holder of the security may deliver the
security to the Government of Eritrea in payment of any debt to the
Government, whereupon such debt shall be discharged for an amount
equivalent to the sum of the outstanding principal amount of the security and
any amounts of unpaid interest and charges that have accrued thereon until the
date of the security is delivered.
(4) The delivery request under sub-Article (3) hereof shall specify that the request
is based on that sub-Article and identify the debt or other obligation that is
being paid to the Government.

(5) After the discharge of the debt, the security shall be marked “redeemed” if it is
a certificated security, or “deleted from the securities account of the holder” if
it is a book-entry.
Article 17: Redeemed Securities
When all payments of principal, interest and other charges on a book-entry Treasury
security are made, all entries concerning the security on the Ledger of National Debt
shall be deleted. Certificates of certificated securities shall be marked “redeemed”.
Article 18: Alteration and Deletion of Entries
Entries on the Ledger of National Debt concerning a book-entry security may be
altered or deleted only at the written request of the person in whose name the entry is
registered. However, errors and omissions may be corrected, provided they are
authenticated by the Head of the Debt Management office.
Article 19: Statements to Security Holders
The Bank of Eritrea shall send each holder of Treasury securities a statement once a
year showing the holder’s position in his securities accounts.
Article 20: Statements to the Minister of Finance
Within one month after each calendar quarter, the Manager of the debt Management
office shall send a report to the Minister of Finance showing all Treasury securities
outstanding at the end of calendar.
Article 21: Audit
Within four months after each fiscal year of the Bank of Eritrea, the Ledger of
national Debt together with its supporting records and documents shall be audited by
an independent auditor appointed by the Board of Directors of the Bank of Eritrea. A
copy of the audit report shall be furnished to the Minister of Finance.
Article 22: Secrecy
Present and past managers of the Debt Management Office and their staff shall keep
secret, and may neither use for personal gain nor permit to be examined by others, any
information that they obtained in the course of their services concerning the Ledger of
national Debt. Such information may be disclosed only to the Bank of Eritrea,
auditors of the Ledger of National Debt, the Ministry of Finance or his authorized
representative and to such other administrative and to judicial authorities as the law
provides.
Violation of these secrecy requirements shall be punishable in accordance with the
provisions of the Penal Code.
Article 23: Authority to Issue Regulations
The Minister of Finance may issue regulations necessary for the implementation of
the provisions of this Proclamation.

Article 24: Effective Date
This Proclamation shall enter into force as of the date of its publication in the Gazette
of Eritrean Laws.
Done at Asmara, this 12th day of August, 1998
Government of Eritrea.
